ratio_decidendi.ratio: A scheme approved by the Supreme Court shall be considered the 'law' under Article 141/142 of the Constitution, and the court can pass suitable directions to enforce it as a mandate, until the enactment of a suitable statute by the Legislatures.
obiter: In some other judgments, this Court gave some more guidelines.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The Court gives its imprimatur to the Witness Protection Scheme prepared by the government, approving it and directing that it comes into effect forthwith. The Court found no reason not to accept the scheme, as it was the comprehensive outcome of collaborative efforts by the Central Government, State Governments, Union Territories, and other stakeholders.
legal_tests_applied: The court's reasoning is grounded in the principle of ensuring a 'Fair Trial', which is undermined if witnesses are threatened or forced to give false evidence.

The court evaluates the state's fulfillment of its 'definite role' and 'salutary duty' to protect witnesses, particularly in sensitive cases, to prevent the trial from being tainted and to assist the court in discovering the truth.
why_appellant_lost: The appellant's (petitioner's) primary goal was achieved, as the court's intervention resulted in the formal implementation of a witness protection scheme. The petition was disposed of not because the petitioner's core argument was rejected, but because the respondent's actions in creating a comprehensive scheme satisfied the petition's underlying objective.
why_respondent_won: The respondent's proposed scheme was accepted because it was the comprehensive 'outcome of the efforts put in by the Central Government with due assistance not only from the State Governments as well as Union Territories but other stakeholders including Police personnel, NALSA and State Legal Services Authorities, High Courts and even civil society.'
The court found 'no reason not to accede to the aforesaid submission of the learned Attorney General and other respondents' due to the collaborative and thorough nature of the scheme's creation.
policy_considerations: The State has a definite role to play in protecting witnesses, especially in sensitive cases involving those in power who wield muscle and money, 'to avert trial getting tainted and derailed and truth becoming a casualty.'

A witness, by giving evidence, 'performs a sacred duty of assisting the court to discover the truth,' and it is the 'salutary duty of every witness who has the knowledge of the commission of the crime, to assist the State in giving evidence.'
If witnesses are threatened or forced to give false evidence, it would not result in a fair trial, as established in the Zahira Habibullah Sheikh case.
